item.title: Cloud computing as a disaster management tool for documentary heritage management
item.description: Archives exist to collect and manage the memory of nations, including documentary heritage management. The transformation of the archives from the physical to digital format is even more imperative in the digital age. The purpose of this paper is to investigate the usage of cloud computing as a disaster management tool for documentary heritage management from the perspective of the National University of Lesotho’s Library (NUL) digitisation project. item.title: Preservation management framework in library and archival institutions
item.description: On a daily basis, organisations, both government and non-government, produce a lot of goods, provide services and create records as evidence of their business transactions. item.title: Preserving and indigenising chieftainship cultural heritage in Lesotho
item.description: This study explored aims and progress of preserving and indigenising chieftainship and the monarch’s cultural heritage, the case of Royal Archives, Museum and Information Centre (RAM) in Lesotho. Evolving in 2006 from the repatriated collection of King Moshoeshoe II, RAM developed into a broad-based facility aimed at indigenising the monarch’s cultural heritage. Key terms are conceptualised. item.title: Safeguarding Basotho heritage
item.description: This paper investigates how the Lesotho National Library Services (LNLS) safeguards Basotho cultural heritage through the Lesotho Collection and the challenges it faces in sustaining effective digital preservation. item.title: Preserving the past, present and future
item.description: Audio-visual recordings generated by public broadcasters contribute to a nation's collection of cultural heritage materials. Broadcasters have a responsibility to ensure that these recordings are preserved for future use to ensure that a nation's historical and cultural assets are preserved. item.title: Preserving language through digital neologisms
item.description: This paper examines the role of neologisms in preserving linguistic knowledge, focusing on how digital platforms, particularly social media, contribute to the creation, dissemination, and preservation of these terms in the digital age. item.title: Language and translation as tools for the archiving and preservation of Indigenous knowledge
item.description: Translation, along with interpreting and prostitution, is said to be one of the oldest professions in the world. item.title: A case for black sartorial history
item.description: In this article, we investigate black sartoriality through oral history, archives, museums, and libraries by focusing on Martin Molefe, the South African black fashion designer.
